task: Prepare a complete English editorial card for the Motux stop in Francisco Pizarro’s1532 expedition, usable as a reusable single-waypoint pattern. Describe the four-day rest from Xerez, retain the distinction between his translated participant account and Markham’s later Motupe identification, and bound chronology without inventing a calendar arrival date. Explain the modern reference location without claiming camp precision. Add attributed coastal-road cultural observations without assigning an ethnic identity. Provide a modern photograph with its supplied credit,licence and access caveats, and a linked regional study with its actual consultation basis and geographic/time limits. Each prose claim must be grounded in the supplied body spans or literal metadata. Evidence gaps must remain visible. Publication requires human approval; do not turn metadata into historic testimony.

seeds.title: Francisco de Xerez: four-day rest at Motux
seeds.text:
The Spaniards rested at
Motux for four days, and, during that time, the Governor
saw some portion of the inhabited country belonging to the
chief, which appeared to be extensive, and to include a

fertile valley.

gaps.text: The selected Xerez passage gives a four-day rest but no exact Motux arrival or departure date. Its narrative position falls after San Miguel departure24September1532 and before Caxamalca arrival15November1532.
Markham identifies Motux with Motupe, but the supplied sources do not establish exact historic camp coordinates. The modern Motupe point is a reference marker only.
The supplied sources do not establish an ethnic or linguistic identity for the people encountered at Motux. General coastal-road descriptions and a later Mórrope study cannot provide that assignment.

The Commons image item is accessible and declares CC BY-SA4.0; original asset returnedHTTP429 and alternate thumbnailHTTP403. New image bytes, visual contents, capture date,camera GPS and independent municipality permission have not been verified.
The linked study was consulted at official bibliographic-record and abstract level. Its regional,later scope is relevant background only; it cannot be treated as direct testimony about Motux1532.

The evidence is an1872 English translation preserved in a1970 reprint scan and pdftotext extraction with OCR artifacts. It is neither an autograph nor the original Spanish manuscript; Markham editorial notes remain separate from Xerez narrative.
